questions.question: What motivated you to go on exchange? (pick the most important one) *
questions.answer: Academic opportunities

questions.question: Which aspects were crucial to choosing your study destination? *
questions.answer: What kind of courses was available.

questions.question: How would you rate your overall study abroad experience? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Everything was very pleasant and good, except for the University Administration, i.e. the course inrollment and the overall administration.

questions.question: How easy was it to find the information you needed to know upon arrival? *
questions.answer: Very easy. University of Glasgow is very helpful.

questions.question: What assistance, if any, did you receive when you arrived at your study destination? *
questions.answer: All contact information of the relevant student associations, representatives who could help, locations, how to find accommodation, where to find literature, etc.

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the orientation and assistance available to students at your host institution upon arrival? *
Additional comments
questions.answer: Very.

questions.question: How did you find housing? *
questions.answer: I found housing on my own

questions.question: Did you live on campus or off campus? *
questions.answer: Off campus

questions.question: How easy was it to find off campus housing? Any recommendations? *
questions.answer: For me it was quite easy, I joined a Facebook Group and started searching for housing already in May 2022 - a long time prior to the beginning of the exchange (September 2022).

questions.question: What should future exchange students know about living off campus? *
questions.answer: It is good, they should find a Facebook Group, for example, one that says "Danes in Scotland".

questions.question: Overall, how satisfied were you with the housing available to students? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Although it is good, it is almost more expensive than Copenhagen.

questions.question: How easy did you find the registration process at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: The institution handled everything with registration for you.

questions.question: Please describe the registration process at your host institution *
questions.answer: Even though the course enrollment was difficult, the one in charge sent emails all the time, keeping you updated and working hard to get everything done for you.

questions.question: What kind of help was available? *
questions.answer: All kinds, you could call the one in charge, send them an email or visit them at their office.

questions.question: How successful were you in registering for the classes you wanted? *
questions.answer: Not very. It has been said, that the University had difficulties combining the many courses being canceled and the many students accepted. In the end, it turned out well, and I am glad.

questions.question: What advice would you offer to future exchange students about registration at your host institution? *
questions.answer: Be patient. It will turn out in a good way in the end, and don't hesitate to contact the one in charge if i.e. you have preferences or wishes - they do everything they can to fulfill this.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the academic programme at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: Very well structured, the content was good and well balanced.

questions.question: Were you a BA or MA student at UCPH when you were on exchange? *
questions.answer: BA

questions.question: Please elaborate on the level of courses *
questions.answer: I was only allowed to study undergraduate courses.

questions.question: How did the style of teaching at your host institution compare with that of UCPH? *
questions.answer: It was extremely similar.

questions.question: How long were you on exchange? *
questions.answer: 1 semester

questions.question: Please list the courses you were enrolled in during your first semester. *
questions.answer: Land Law, Company Law and Law of Contract.

questions.question: What specific courses would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: Company law and Land Law.

What unexpected costs did you encounter? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What items were more or less expensive than you expected? *
questions.answer: Everything in the service areas is cheaper. The housing and the bills were more expensive than expected - although having in mind, we are in the middle of a war in Europe and an energy crisis.

questions.question: How satisfied were you with the non-academic opportunities (clubs, sports, etc.) at your host institution? *
Additional comments:
questions.answer: It is amazing how the sports clubs and associations and other student associations are handled and given so many resources. There is some kind of non-academic social fellowship for any one!

questions.question: What kinds of cultural, athletic and social activities were available for students at your host institution? *
questions.answer: The gym, Tennis, swimming, the law society, the whisky society, the nordic society, and Erasmus society.

questions.question: Which non -academic activities would you recommend to future exchange students? Why? *
questions.answer: All of them.

questions.question: What do you recommend other visiting students see or do on their weekends or holidays? *
questions.answer: Everything cultural, Glasgow has an amazing unique stage for upcoming artists in the city with a lot of happenings, live music, and art fairs. And the highlands! Never not go to the highlands.

questions.question: How easy was it to adjust to the local culture of your exchange site? *
questions.answer: Very easy. Glasgow has a hashtag "People make Glasgow". They are the most welcoming, helpful and warm people.

questions.question: Do you have any tips for socializing with local students?
questions.answer: Join the sports clubs and the student associations.

questions.question: What, if any, cultural differences did you find particularly challenging? *
questions.answer: None.

questions.question: What parts of the culture did you most appreciate? *
questions.answer: The People Make Glasgow concept.

questions.question: What are the three most important things you would tell a UCPH student who is going to your host institution on exchange? *
questions.answer: Be prepared to become friends with everyone, that the academic level is as high as UCPH and that the cost of living is similar as well.

questions.question: Is there any other information that you think might prove useful to future exchange students attending your host institution? *
questions.answer: UK is no longer part of the EU, thus it is important to remember to fix your VISA if you want to go.

questions.question: What was the most rewarding part of your exchange experience? *
questions.answer: The people, the good academic feedback and the networking.

questions.question: What was the greatest challenge during the exchange? *
questions.answer: Taking notes during seminars, since the professors talked fast and very Scottish - but that was only in the beginning.

questions.question: Any other comments?
questions.answer: It was a wonderful experience, and I can only give UofG my warmest recommendations.

questions.question: Do you agree to share your travel report with other fellow students? *
questions.answer: Yes
